haiku-low.q1: If unfiltered row_count is 10,000 or fewer, the server returns the CSV in the click response. Above 10,000, the click records an export, a background job builds it, and an emailed link follows.
haiku-low.q2: The click returns the active export with HTTP 200 and starts nothing. The page shows a notice that the new filters were not used; the user clicks again after it finishes.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link works for 86,400 seconds (24 hours). The exports bucket rule deletes each file 7 days after it was written. Downloads get 900-second signed URLs.
haiku-low.q4: Up to three attempts, retried automatically after 60 and 300 seconds. After the third failure, the user gets a report_export_failed email and the page shows the error summary.
haiku-low.q5: The read replica. Report rows are never read from the primary database, which holds the export records.
haiku-low.q6: In the report_exports table on the primary database. The page polls the latest-export endpoint every 5 seconds while queued or running, and on tab focus; reopening fetches it again.
haiku-low.q7: It reads 5,000 rows per page by keyset paging from the replica. The Writer sends 16 MB buffers as multipart upload parts, keeping only one buffer and one page in memory. No local file is written.
haiku-low.q8: Parts already sent stay in the open multipart upload. The next attempt aborts that upload and restarts from row 1 under its own key. Unlinked objects remain until the 7-day rule deletes them.
haiku-low.q9: Filters and cols are stored on the export record at click time. The job payload carries only export_id, and the job reads filters and cols from that record.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) covering queued or running rows. The losing insert is rejected, and that request reads and returns the active export.
haiku-low.q11: The file must be complete via complete_multipart, and the attempt's CAS from running to done must apply. Repeat runs after done or failed return without work, so no second file or email.
haiku-low.q12: If the connection drops, the browser discards the partial file. What the server does when a small export fails partway is NOT STATED.

sonnet.q1: Chosen by the report's total unfiltered row_count: 10,000 or fewer goes inline, more goes to a background job. Inline: the response body is the CSV (text/csv, attachment), streamed from the replica, nothing stored; the browser fetches it as a blob and saves it on success. Large: the click records an export, returns 202 at once with export_id/state/filters/cols/created_at; the job writes the CSV to object storage, the page shows progress, and the user gets an email with a signed download link valid 24 hours (and a Download button on the page).
sonnet.q2: The partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) for queued/running rows rejects the insert. The server runs the stale check first; if the active export is stale (over 2 hours) it is marked failed and the insert is retried once. Otherwise the active export is returned with HTTP 200 and nothing new starts. If its filters differ from the page's, the page shows a notice that the new filters were not used and the user can start a new export when it finishes. There is no cancel.
sonnet.q3: The emailed link is valid 86,400 seconds (24 hours). The exports bucket rule deletes each file 7 days after it was written. No cleanup job exists. (The page's Download button issues a fresh 900-second signed URL; after 7 days it shows expired.)
sonnet.q4: Up to 3 attempts, with 60 s wait before attempt 2 and 300 s before attempt 3. After attempt 3 fails (including a 30-minute timeout or a dead worker), the final-failure handler marks the export failed with error_summary 'timed out on attempt 3' or 'failed on attempt 3', aborts any open upload, and emails the user 'report_export_failed' (report_name, page_url, error_summary). The page shows the error_summary and a Start again button. If the handler itself fails, it later shows 'failed: stalled' with no email.
sonnet.q5: The read replica only, never the primary. (Export records are kept on the primary.)
sonnet.q6: In the export record (report_exports table) on the primary database, in the state column. The page polls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest every 5 seconds while queued or running, stops at a final state, and refetches when the tab regains focus. On a later visit it loads the latest export on page load and shows it in whatever state it is in. The browser keeps nothing; the server holds all state.
sonnet.q7: It streams: the Reader reads 5,000-row keyset pages from the replica, the Writer turns them into CSV bytes, and when a 16 MB buffer fills it is uploaded as one multipart part, then cleared. Memory is one 16 MB buffer plus one page of rows; etags are kept in memory and no local file is written. About 900 MB of CSV is about 60 parts (limit 10,000). It needs at least 1,100 rows/s to finish within 1,800 s (throughput gate; whether it passes is unknown until run).
sonnet.q8: Each attempt starts again from the first row (from the beginning). The next attempt, when it claims the row, aborts the earlier attempt's upload_id (ignoring already-gone errors) and clears it. Each attempt writes under its own key (...-attemptN.csv), so attempts never collide. If the worker died after complete_multipart but before the CAS to done, that finished object is never linked or served and stays until the 7-day rule deletes it. A part upload is retried up to 3 times within the attempt before it fails. Uploads orphaned before upload_id was saved are discarded by the bucket after 24 hours.
sonnet.q9: They are stored in the filters and cols columns of the export record (report_exports row on the primary DB), taken from the page view's address strings in the POST. The enqueue payload holds only the export_id; the job reads filters and cols from the record, not from the page.
sonnet.q10: A partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) covering only rows in state queued or running, in the database. The insert by one request succeeds and the other is rejected.
sonnet.q11: The email is sent only by the attempt whose CAS from running to done applied (attempt still equals its own), which happens only after complete_multipart succeeded and the object is visible at the attempt's own key. The email is then built with a signed URL for object_key. On a repeat run: the handler loads the row and returns without doing anything if state is done (or failed), so one file and one email. A duplicate of the same or an older attempt matches no CAS claim and returns; a CAS that does not apply sends nothing.
sonnet.q12: If the connection drops partway, the browser discards the partial file because the button fetches the response as a blob and saves it only if the fetch finishes without a network error. The user sees an error and can click again. Nothing is stored on the server. The document does not say more about server-side mid-stream failures (e.g. replica failure during inline streaming).
